radar.summary_en: The article presents cameo, a local HTTP proxy that routes selected subagent model names to third-party Anthropic-compatible endpoints while forwarding other traffic to the original provider. The goal is to expose cheaper models directly as Claude Code subagents and avoid the overhead of another harness's history interface. TOML examples define general-purpose and Read/Grep/Glob-only exploration agents. The author reports more frequent delegation, but supplies no cost, latency, success-rate or quality comparison; frequency alone does not establish savings. Earlier cross-harness permission approval is a motivation for changing designs, not proof that cameo is secure. Project links are visible, but code, runtime and provider behavior were not inspected. Codex compatibility is likewise an author observation at that time. Treat this as an integration design whose versions, credential routing, permission isolation and reliability still require testing.

Record stores attempts and failures; Ledger retains separately rechecked intermediate lemmas or counterexamples. The emphasis is verified knowledge state rather than longer chat history. The article relays five theoretical results and roughly 100–1,000 model calls. This review did not inspect the original paper, companion proofs or implementation, so mathematical results remain reported claims. The article itself distinguishes expert checking, independent replication, peer review and formal theorem verification. Four page images remain uninspected. Separating failed attempts from reusable knowledge is a useful lead for long-running agents, but assessing the underlying research requires original proofs, baselines, ablations and a reproducible workflow rather than this summary alone.

radar.summary_en: Moongazer RL separates answer generation from model updates to reduce step-by-step waiting in LLM reinforcement learning. It combines vLLM generation, Unsloth/TRL LoRA updates and verifiers environments for tasks and scoring. Bounded queues, model-version tags and truncated importance sampling manage stale asynchronous data and distribution mismatch. The single-RTX-5090 example uses one-turn math questions, bf16 generation and a learner loading the base model in four bits, with a pinned commit, configuration excerpts and log fields. The author reports completing 12 steps and 440 rollouts in 473 seconds, with 28.7 GB peak GPU memory. Crucially, 98.3% describes overlap between learning and model-call time intervals, not GPU utilization or simultaneous GPU-kernel execution; the learner still waits for 61.8% of total runtime. The article acknowledges that it has neither a matched synchronous comparison nor an evaluation of accuracy improvement. These observations therefore support only a small-scale working-pipeline claim, not frontier capability or general speedup. This review reads the newly saved body without running the example or independently inspecting linked code, raw logs or images.
radar.summary_zh: Moongazer RL 把回答生成與模型更新分開，嘗試減少 LLM 強化學習逐步等待的成本。文章以 vLLM 生成、Unsloth／TRL 更新 LoRA，並由 verifiers 環境負責題目與評分；有限容量佇列、模型世代標記及截斷重要性取樣，用來管理非同步資料的陳舊與偏差。單張 RTX 5090 範例採用單輪數學題，生成端使用 bf16，學習端以四位元載入模型，並提供固定提交、設定片段與日誌欄位。作者報告十二步、四百四十次生成在四百七十三秒完成，GPU 記憶體峰值為 28.7 GB。值得注意的是，98.3% 指學習與模型呼叫區間在時間上重疊，不能當成 GPU 使用率或核心同時運算率；學習端仍有 61.8% 時間等待。文中也承認沒有同步方式的同條件比較或準確率提升評估，因此只能支持小規模流程可運作的主張，不能證明前沿能力或普遍加速。此次查閱重新保存的正文，未執行範例，也未獨立檢視連結程式、原始日誌及圖像。

radar.summary_en: This case examines bias when human-corrected model output becomes the reference for comparing systems. The author withdrew an Apple-versus-Whisper CER comparison of 5.4% versus 33.6%: 53% of the Apple-derived reference's 335 rows were untouched, while selecting corrected passages introduces an opposing selection bias. A later 17.9% versus 27.2% comparison also changes cropping and row selection, so it neither isolates reference bias nor establishes a fair ranking. The inspected designed report-excerpt panel and chart support the retraction presentation, not authenticated raw records. A ten-minute blind reference and rerun remain unfinished. Provenance and reporting controls are useful ideas, although the example mistakes absence of an intersecting source for proof of independent annotation. Treat this as a warning for language-model evaluation and agent reporting; other materials and cited studies remain unverified.

radar.summary_en: PathScope asks which combinations of host settings let an ordinary user reach higher privileges and which remediation would affect the most paths. Rust collects host facts; an LLM turns irregular configuration text into proposed JSON facts. Source lines, quotations and fields are checked before Prolog derives paths with reasons. Ranking first counts the simple paths containing each edge, then applies fuzzy reasoning to the affected-path proportion, target importance and ease of action. This is not a minimum-cut algorithm, and what-if remediation changes copied facts only. Examples reject invented paths, wrong line numbers and unconfirmed scripts, but validation cannot recover LLM omissions, and aliases or variable expansion remain limited. Disabling the LLM removes paths derived from sudoers and cron contents. The author reports checking Claude responses only on synthetic data, without detection rates, false-positive rates, performance comparisons or complete test artifacts; the seven fuzzy rules and ease-of-action table are not fully supplied. The value is separation of responsibilities and traceability, not proof of comprehensive host security. This review uses the newly saved body; linked packages, product pages and visual presentation were not independently verified, and no commands were executed.
radar.summary_zh: PathScope 想回答一般使用者能透過哪些設定組合抵達高權限，以及先修哪一處較有影響。它以 Rust 收集端點事實，讓 LLM 把不規則設定轉成 JSON 候選，再核對原始行、引用與欄位，通過後交給 Prolog 推論附帶理由的路徑。排序先計算每條邊涉及多少簡單路徑，再以影響比例、目標重要度與操作容易度進行模糊推論；這不是最小割演算法，修補模擬也只改事實副本。文章提供拒絕捏造路徑、錯誤行號及未確認腳本的例子，但驗證不能找回模型漏讀的內容，別名和變數展開也受限。關閉 LLM 時，sudoers 與 cron 內容導出的路徑便不會出現。作者只報告以 Claude 檢查合成資料，沒有偵測率、誤報率、效能比較或完整測試產物，七條模糊規則與容易度表也未完整公開。因此價值在責任分工與可追溯設計，不能據此確認真實端點的安全完整性。此次依重新保存的正文評讀；連結套件、產品頁及視覺呈現未獨立驗證，沒有執行其中指令。

radar.summary_en: This tutorial follows MoE tensor shapes from per-token routing through top-k selection, dispatch, combination and restoration of token order. Its eight-expert example selects E4 and E6 with weights near 0.599 and 0.401. It distinguishes total parameters from active compute, balancing loss from capacity, and algorithmic FLOPs from communication-inclusive latency; more experts do not proportionally reduce memory or wall-clock time. It also separates the original LSTM-based architecture from later Transformer FFN usage. The pure-Python function demonstrates only top-k selection and stable softmax, not distributed dispatch, backpropagation or training. These formulas and boundaries are educationally useful but introduce no model-quality or speed experiment. Text and code were read, not executed; diagrams and cited papers/docs remain unverified. Use it to plan hardware-specific measurement of communication, overflow, expert batch sizes and end-to-end performance.

top5.summary_en: This operational case report describes a local-LLM website workflow on one Mac Studio. A measurement process handles models sequentially; an operations process checks results every ten minutes, with agents running between measurements to reduce memory contention. Six roles cover operations, writing, translation, design, mail triage and repair. Deterministic checks validate numeric ranges and publication decisions, substitute templates and roll back failed deployments. The author reports that safeguards blocked an impossible throughput value and accidental removal of an existing model, but also delayed valid results and required human recovery. None of four attempted code repairs was merged: three hit output limits, and the later attempt identified the cause but failed tests. The absence of per-item human approval therefore does not mean the system is maintenance-free or error-free. Role-test scores, aggregate error rates and a control group are missing; the architecture image and linked operating logs were not inspected. The transferable value is layered checking and failure isolation, with reliability still requiring fuller evidence.

top5.summary_en: This local-inference benchmark separates Magnitude’s advertised speedup from a 16GB M5 Mac workload. Using the same LFM2.5 GGUF and medians of three runs for each of three short prompts, the author reports 88.9–97.0 tokens/s for Magnitude and 103.7–105.1 for newer llama.cpp. Different hardware, models and 64K-context conditions are outside this comparison. Magnitude loaded successfully only in the first session; 36 subsequent attempts across two sessions failed its memory gate, so reversed-order sessions do not provide fully paired engine measurements. Python benchmark statements are supplied, but nested indentation is lost in the saved text and raw run logs are absent. Its fallback substitutes streaming chunk counts when API token usage is absent, requiring receipt-level verification. DSpark cannot be disabled, preventing isolation of speculative decoding from kernel tuning. The fresh extraction exposes the code statements, but does not preserve executable indentation or recover historical bytes. Conclusions remain limited to the stated machine, versions and short prompts; answer quality, long-context behavior and cited external reports were not independently checked.
top5.summary_zh: 這篇本機推論技術實測，把 Magnitude 的兩倍速宣稱與十六 GB M5 Mac 的使用情境分開。作者以相同 LFM2.5 GGUF、三種短提示，各跑三次取中位數，報告 Magnitude 每秒八十八點九至九十七個詞元，llama.cpp 新版約一百零三點七至一百零五點一個。這不能反駁其他硬體、大模型或六十四 K 長脈絡的結果，因為測試條件不同。更大的實務限制是，Magnitude 只有第一個工作階段成功載入，後兩階段共三十六次被記憶體門檻拒絕，因此換順序後並未取得完整配對比較。正文附 Python 量測片段，但保存文字遺失巢狀縮排，且缺少逐次紀錄；若 API 未回傳詞元用量，程式會把串流片段數當作詞元數，仍需核對實際回應。DSpark 無法關閉，也無法分離核心調校與投機解碼的貢獻。此次擷取能辨識程式內容，卻未保留可直接執行的縮排，也未恢復舊來源原始位元組。結論應限於作者報告的機器、版本與短提示，不能推廣成所有平台的引擎排名；回答品質、長脈絡及外部引用仍待驗證。
